thread.title: 7 Ways To Play Intel, Nvidia And Other Top Chip Stocks

author: NANCY GONDO
title: 7 Ways To Play Intel, Nvidia And Other Top Chip Stocks
text:
Semiconductors were among sector funds advancing Wednesday as Analog Devices ( ADI ) reversed to a 2% gain after a beat-and-raise earnings report.
X The chipmaker delivered fiscal Q2 results that beat on both the top and bottom lines. The company also offered guidance above views . Shares cleared a 96.95 buy point of a flat base intraday and were trading just below the entry.
VanEck Vectors Semiconductor ( SMH ) and iShares PHLX Semiconductor ( SOXX ) rose 0.4% and 0.5% respectively. Analog Devices is a top 10 holding in both funds, with a 4.7% weighting in SMH and 4.2% in SOXX. Other top 10 chip stocks moving included Intel ( INTC ), up 0.7%; Micron Technology ( MU ), down 0.2%; and Nvidia ( NVDA ), up 0.9%. Micron was trading below a 63.52 cup-base buy point initially cleared Tuesday on a bullish analyst report .
SMH and SOXX are working on the right side of their respective bases. The ideal buy point for SMH is 114.65; it's 198.94 for SOXX. The chip sector had come under some recent pressure amid concerns about weak smartphone chip sales. For instance, Apple ( AAPL ) chip supplier Broadcom ( AVGO ) last month lowered the top end of its current-quarter sales outlook. Taiwan Semiconductor ( TSM ) also recently cited weak smartphone sales.

Please contact customer service CLOSE The two largest semiconductor ETFs in terms of assets are $1.7 billion SOXX and $1.3 billion SMH. SOXX, which tracks the PHLX Semiconductor Sector Index, will turn 17 years old in July. Six-year-old SMH tracks the MVIS U.S. Listed Semiconductor 25 Index.
SOXX's 10.7% year-to-date return through Tuesday, according to Morningstar Inc., was well ahead of the S&P 500's 1% advance. Chips have trended higher over the past two years before stalling in late November. SOXX's average annual returns over the past three, five and 10 years of 24.4%, 25.8% and 14% outpaced the S&P 500's 10.8%, 12.6% and 9.1% gains. SMH delivered 23.3% and 24.6% over the past three and five years.
Other Chip Plays Other unleveraged semiconductor ETFs include PowerShares Dynamic Semiconductor ( PSI ), with $348.3 million in assets, and SPDR S&P Semiconductor ( XSD ), with $326 million.
Below are a few ideas for those who prefer leveraged plays, which target double or triple the performance or inverse performance of the underlying index. Be aware that these tend to be more volatile than their nonleveraged counterparts and usually have higher expense ratios.
Direxion Daily Semiconductor Bull 3x Shares ( SOXL ), with $853.4 million in assets, seeks triple the return of the PHLX Semiconductor Sector Index. ProShares Ultra Semiconductors ( USD ) ($80.3 million) aims for two times the daily performance of the Dow Jones U.S. Semiconductors Index.
